name: XCarnival XNFT withdrawn-collateral order reuse
summary: XNFT.withdrawNFT() returned a pledged NFT without closing or invalidating the pledge order, so getOrderDetail kept reporting the collateral and P2Controller.borrowAllowed kept approving borrows against it. The attacker pledged one BAYC, withdrew it, re-pledged it into a new order, and repeated the cycle to open 83 simultaneously borrowable orders backed by the same token.
notes: The proxy's only Upgraded event, emitted in its creation transaction, selected 0x39360ac1239a0b98cb8076d4135d0f72b7fd9909; the EIP-1967 implementation slot still holds that address at block 15028860.

Six borrow transactions moved 2,988 ETH out of the xETH pool 0xb38707e31c813f832ef71c70731ed80b45b85b2d, whose balance falls from 3,014.418576385059098519 ETH at block 15028860 to 26.418576385059098519 ETH at block 15029010; the four attacker exploit contracts forward exactly 1,980 + 540 + 288 + 180 = 2,988 ETH to the attacker EOA. Widely reported figures of 3,087 ETH are the attacker EOA balance after the campaign, which also contains pre-attack funds. DefiLlama's nearest ETH observation to the incident timestamp is at 1656244505. The attacker returned 1,467 ETH to the XCarnival deployer the following day; recovery is not netted out of the exploit-time loss.
